The H-RGC material is a 6-layer, symmetric and thin radar absorber with reflective surfaces on both sides.
Carbon black and graphene nanoplatelets were used as the conductive fillers to produce the rubber composites for the reflective surface and hybrid layer.
The RSA measurements were conducted in the 6-17 GHz frequency band, with angular coverage from 0 to 360 degrees in 3-degree steps.
Both the H-RGC and M-REM materials were able to achieve a reduction of around 20 dBsm in their RSA performance.
The best RSA values for M-REM were obtained between 24-72 degrees, while for H-RGC, it was in the range of 21-72 degrees.
The RSA values improved as the frequency bandwidth increased for both the H-RGC and M-REM materials.
At 12 GHz, the lowest absorption value was 42.6743 dBsm for M-REM and 42.9219 dBsm for H-RGC.
The similarity and match between the measurement results of the H-RGC and M-REM materials demonstrate the validity of the H-RGC design.
The H-RGC material is designed for potential use in systems such as ships and military land vehicles to reduce their radar cross-section area.
The multilayer design with reflective surfaces and the incorporation of conductive fillers contribute to the broadband performance of the H-RGC material.
The RSA values show a strong angular dependence, with the best performance observed between 24-72 degrees for M-REM and 21-72 degrees for H-RGC.
The ticari M-REM material is designed to reduce the radar cross-section area of military land vehicles (tank, truck, ship, etc.) and is currently commercially available.
The H-RGC material was produced using a 200-ton capacity hydraulic press with a special molding method, resulting in a 5.7±0.3 mm thick composite structure.
The vulcanization of the H-RGC material was performed at 180°C for 22 minutes, and the samples were conditioned at 23±2°C and 50±5% relative humidity for 24 hours before testing.

The RSA measurements were conducted in a closed-field laboratory environment at a distance of 26 m, using a tomography-based near-field to far-field transformation algorithm developed by TUBITAK Bilgem.
